thread.title: Duck and Cover if These 3 Stocks Slip

title: Duck and Cover if These 3 Stocks Slip
text:
The Dow’s Gains for This Year Could Be Toast if These 3 Stocks Slump By Oct. 11, 2018 12:51 p.m. ET Order Reprints Print Article Boeing has the heaviest weighting in the Dow. Joel Arbaje; Source Photos: Copy Negative, and Sandra Kaas Text size
After Wednesday’s stock market slide, a look under the hood of the Dow Jones Industrial Average shows that the index’s advance so far this year, now about 3%, remains a narrowly fought battle.
Just three stocks are effectively responsible for the gain, and if they falter, the index could drop into the red for 2018. On Wednesday, the Dow fell 831.83 points, or 3.1%, to 25598.74.
Which companies in the venerable index have been the big winners and losers has actually changed little over the past three weeks. As of Wednesday’s close, Boeing (ticker: BA), UnitedHealth Group (UNH), and Apple (AAPL) had contributed 1,284.39 points to the index this year.
How’s that, with the Dow up only 879.52 points at that point?
There are 16 losers year to date in the Dow, out of 30 stocks, so it isn’t as if there is a lopsided number of losing stocks. Instead, it’s the nature of the Dow: Because two of the biggest losers are also among the top five in index weight—along with the three mentioned above—they count for more. A lot more. Newsletter Sign-up
The big losers are Goldman Sachs (GS), with a 5.72% weight, and 3M (MMM), with 5.4%. As of Wednesday, Goldman had sucked 221.28 points out of the Dow, while 3M had weakened it by 188.35. Those figures were 116 and 130, respectively, back on Sept. 21.
That day, when the Dow was at 26743.50, the same three leading stocks had contributed 1968 points, higher than the total advance of 1938 points at the time.
The Dow is calculated simply based on the stock prices of its 30 components, so companies whose shares trade at higher levels, such as Boeing, at about $347 per share, matter much more than, say, a company like Cisco Systems (CSCO), whose shares trade around $46. More on the Market
